# Results — Study 301 (Triple-RSI) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The canonical Triple-RSI
recipe — buy at the close when RSI(5) < 30 **and** RSI is down three days in a row
**and** RSI three days ago was < 60 **and** close > SMA(200); exit at the close when
RSI(5) > 50 — run on SPY (and QQQ, IWM, DIA for breadth) with daily bars since 1993–2000.
Pinned against a **random-direction control** on the *same* entry bars, re-run with a
conservative **next-open** fill, and split pre/post-2010. As-of **2026-06-17**; match the
per-tape fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | Days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| SPY | 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-17 | 8,403 | `b891c5df8fc1` |
| QQQ | 1999-03-10 → 2026-06-17 | 6,861 | `422820470ec7` |
| IWM | 2000-05-26 → 2026-06-17 | 6,553 | `ec8b35339b52` |

## The headline — SPY, canonical recipe, close fill, gross

| Period | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | skew | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **All (1993–2026)** | 118 | **88.1%** | **+132.8** | −1.59 | **+5.07** |
| Pre-2010 | 43 | 90.7% | +179.0 | +0.53 | +6.33 |
| Post-2010 | 75 | 86.7% | +106.3 | −2.06 | **+3.11** |
| Random-direction control (all) | 118 | 61.9% | +47.9 | −0.20 | +2.57 |

- The Triple-RSI gross expectancy on SPY is **+132.8 bps/trade** at HAC *t* = **+5.07** —
  comfortably above the inference bar (|t| ≥ 2), firmly in **REAL** territory.
- It **beats the random control** by **+84.9 bps/trade** (132.8 − 47.9). The random arm is
  positive too (equity drift + the exit's selection effect lift all comers), but the
  Triple-RSI conditions add a large, clear extra tilt.
- The **88.1% win-rate** is real, and close to the marketed "90%" (pre-2010 was 90.7%).
  But see the win-rate-illusion section: a high hit-rate is not the edge.
- **No publication collapse:** post-2010 the mean is smaller (+106.3 vs +179.0) but still
  strongly significant (*t* = +3.11). The signal is durable, not arbitraged away.

## Look-ahead check — conservative next-open fill

The published rule fills at the signal bar's **close**, which uses the closing price to
both *form* the signal and *enter* the trade. Re-running with entry at the **next bar's
open** removes any same-bar advantage:

| Fill | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Close (canonical) | 118 | 88.1% | +132.8 | +5.07 |
| **Next open (conservative)** | 118 | 85.6% | **+109.7** | **+4.22** |

The edge survives the honest fill (*t* = +4.22). It is **not** a same-bar-close artefact.

## The win-rate illusion — what a 90% hit-rate is actually worth

A "take the bounce" exit (sell as soon as RSI recovers) mechanically produces many small
wins and rare large losses. On a **pure-coin synthetic tape (reversion = 0)** the *same*
rule with no real signal still prints:

| Synthetic tape | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | skew | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Martingale (reversion = 0) | 507 | **62.3%** | **−34.6** | −1.65 | −1.15 |
| Strong reversion (0.50) | 192 | 73.4% | +103.4 | −1.07 | +5.07 |

The martingale wins **62% of trades with a *negative* mean and t below the bar** — proof
that the win-rate alone says nothing about expectancy. On SPY the win-rate is high *and*
the mean is real; the point is that the marketing number ("90% wins!") is the wrong thing
to look at. The real-tape skew (−1.6) is the same tell: the losses, when they come, are
large (worst SPY trade −7.4%, best +7.8%).

## Could you trade it? — the cost sweep (SPY, canonical, net)

With only ~3.5 trades/yr, per-trade costs barely register:

| round-trip cost | net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* | win-rate | ann. estimate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | +132.8 | +5.07 | 88.1% | +4.69%/yr |
| 2.0 bps | +130.8 | +4.99 | 88.1% | +4.62%/yr |
| 5.0 bps | +127.8 | +4.88 | 88.1% | +4.52%/yr |
| 10.0 bps | +122.8 | +4.69 | 87.3% | +4.34%/yr |

*Annualised estimate = mean\_bps × trades/yr ÷ 100; a naive sum, not a compounding backtest.*

The cost axis is **not** where this strategy dies — the per-trade edge is far too large.
It dies on **capacity**: 118 trades in 33.4 years is **3.5 trades/yr**, with a ~4.8-day
average hold, so the strategy is in the market only **~7% of the time**. The ~+4.7%/yr it
contributes is real but it leaves capital idle 93% of the time, and SPY buy-and-hold
returned **+10.8%/yr** over the same window. As a standalone system the "90% win-rate
machine" earns roughly **half of just holding the index**.

## Without the 200-SMA trend filter

Dropping condition (4) more than doubles the trade count and the signal stays strong:

| Variant | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Canonical (+ SMA200 filter) | 118 | 88.1% | +132.8 | +5.07 |
| No trend filter | 278 | 83.5% | +162.0 | +7.05 |

The filter is not load-bearing here — the oversold-bounce edge exists with or without it
(and dropping it triples the trades to ~8/yr, still thin).

## Pooled basket (SPY + QQQ + IWM + DIA), close fill, gross

| | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | skew | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Triple-RSI rule** | 492 | **78.9%** | **+110.8** | −0.99 | **+8.28** |
| Random-direction control | 492 | 58.7% | +37.1 | −0.79 | +3.93 |

Pooled HAC *t* = **+8.28**, excess over random **+73.7 bps/trade** — the signal is
broad-based across the four index ETFs, not a SPY-only fluke.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is a faithful detector

On a deterministic synthetic daily tape the same engine recovers the edge **only when
short-term anti-persistence is planted**, confirming the rule is a faithful mean-reversion
harvester (and not a number-printer):

| Planted reversion | rule − coin (bps/trade) | rule HAC *t* | signal? |
|---|--:|--:|:--:|
| −0.10 (momentum) | negative | < 0 | no |
| 0.00 (martingale) | ≈ noise | −1.15 | no (|t| < 2) |
| +0.25 | positive | +0.26 | borderline |
| +0.50 (strong reversion) | +62.9 | +5.07 | yes |

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** SPY gross +132.8 bps/trade, HAC *t* = +5.07 (post-2010 +3.11);
  survives a next-open fill (+4.22) and beats a random-direction control by +84.9 bps;
  pooled across four ETFs *t* = +8.28. The oversold bounce is a real, durable effect.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Not a cost story (survives 10 bps at *t* = +4.69) — a
  **capacity** story: 3.5 trades/yr, ~7% time in market, ~+4.7%/yr vs SPY's +10.8%/yr
  buy-and-hold. A genuine but capital-starved overlay, not a standalone system.
- **A 90% win-rate money machine? — BUSTED.** The 88% win-rate is genuine but it is the
  wrong number: under the same exit a pure coin wins 62% with a negative mean, and the
  real tape's −1.6 skew confirms the win-rate hides rare large losses. A high hit-rate is
  not an edge, and this one underperforms the index it trades.
